t: None of the funds provided in this Act shall be available for the implementation or execution of programs the obligations for which are in excess of $60,000,000 in fiscal year 1980 for the “Offshore Oil Pollution Compensation Fund.”

fable.w: This is an appropriations limitation capping obligations for the Offshore Oil Pollution Compensation Fund. The tempting reading is that a compensation fund implies claims by outside parties, but the text only restricts spending and establishes no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: None of the funds provided in this Act shall be available for the implementation or execution of programs the obligations for which are in excess of $60,000,000 in fiscal year 1980

qwen_block.w: This section is a budgetary limitation that restricts the amount of funds available for a specific program. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a federal decision is made. It is purely a financial constraint on federal spending.
qwen_block.s: None of the funds provided in this Act shall be available for the implementation or execution of programs the obligations for which are in excess of $60,000,000 in fiscal year 1980 for the “Offshore Oil Pollution Compensation Fund.”

opus.w: This section only caps fiscal year 1980 obligations for the Offshore Oil Pollution Compensation Fund. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue over a federal decision. The fund's name suggests that outside parties might file claims, but this section creates no such process, and applying for compensation would not count as participation anyway.
opus.s: None of the funds provided in this Act shall be available for the implementation or execution of programs the obligations for which are in excess of $60,000,000 in fiscal year 1980
opus.b: Step 1: This is a cap on how much money can be spent. Someone might read "Offshore Oil Pollution Compensation Fund" as hinting at claims by people outside the government, but the section sets up no claims process, consultation, hearing or right to sue. It only limits obligations.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a fiscal constraint limiting the amount of funds that can be obligated for a specific program. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. The mention of a fund name does not constitute a participation mechanism.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds provided in this Act shall be available for the implementation or execution of programs the obligations for which are in excess of $60,000,000 in fiscal year 1980 for the “Offshore Oil Pollution Compensation Fund.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Offshore Oil Pollution Compensation Fund" implies some form of public participation or compensation process. However, the text itself is purely a fiscal limitation on the use of appropriated funds. It does not describe any process for consultation, comment, hearing, or coordination with outside parties. It simply sets a spending cap.
